title: Specify needs
description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options and preparing a business case, which may weigh the benefits of addressing these needs against expected costs, risks and other requirements, considering the public good arising from meeting those needs and the implications for respondents, users and other stakeholders. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Specify needs' phase requires understanding data requirements from stakeholders, analyzing needs, evaluating the public good versus costs/risks, and participating in the initial stages of the statistical production process. The Junior Evaluation Officer is implicated because they 'provide support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gather and acquire information and analyze databases', and 'participate as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies related to programs, policies and initiatives.' Their familiarity with evaluation processes and gathering/reviewing program requirements aligns with this phase's emphasis on identifying and documenting needs for new or changed statistical business processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 is implicated because, under guidance, they 'participate in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers' and 'participate in the analysis of data and suggest possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures.' They identify statistical trends and developments, which is essential for defining potential new statistical needs and ensuring the relevance of outputs to user requirements, which is central to this GSBPM phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst provides key support in identifying and clarifying needs through 'supporting the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods' and by 'discuss[ing] data requirements with operations managers ... other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.' Their role in translating user needs into analysis-ready requirements is directly implicated in this phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer is implicated as they 'liaise with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.' Their feedback ensures the needs phase incorporates necessary metadata considerations and that initial requirements are consistent with metadata standards.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer participates in 'meet[ings] with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur,' and 'participate[s] on data collection and operations teams.' Their operational perspectives contribute to feasibility, cost, and risk assessment in the needs specification process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is relevant at this phase through their experience interpreting client information requests, providing 'consultative services to users', and participating on production teams. Their perspective contributes to understanding user needs and ensures the public good and stakeholder impacts are carefully considered.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Identify needs
description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. It may be triggered by a new information request from users, an environmental change such as a reduced budget, a periodic review, or respondent feedback. Action plans from evaluations of previous iterations of the production cycle (including from respondent feedback) or from other programmes might provide an input to this sub-process. It also includes consideration of practice amongst other (national and international) statistical organisations producing similar data and the methods used by those organisations.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process requires initial investigation to determine statistical needs and evaluate the context triggering new requirements. The Junior Evaluation Officer undertakes tasks like 'conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data', and participates 'as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies', directly supporting the investigation and identification of needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 engages in 'identifying statistical trends and developments' and 'participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams', which correlates with the investigation of emerging needs, changes in context, and best practices considered in this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Junior Data Analysts provide support in investigation by 'attending meetings ... to gather data/information', 'organizing and consolidating information relevant to defined objectives of studies', and possessing knowledge of data sources and methods—skills necessary for initial needs research.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Consult and confirm needs
description: This sub-process focuses on consulting with the internal and external stakeholders and confirming in detail the needs for the statistics. A good understanding of user needs is required so that the statistical organisation knows not only what it is expected to deliver, but also when, how, and perhaps most importantly, why. For the second and subsequent iterations of this sub-process, the main focus will be on determining whether previously identified needs have changed. This detailed understanding of user needs is the critical part of this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process requires consulting stakeholders and confirming requirements. The Junior Evaluation Officer's communication skills, such as 'Speaking skills are required to discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues' and participation in 'interviews, focus groups and discussions with ... clients', make them directly implicated in this detailed confirmation process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is involved in 'interpreting client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations', and 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users.' Their consultative functions help in detailing and confirming requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Economist/Sociologist 2 given their liaison activities—'liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications', and 'provides data and assistance to users'—are critical for ongoing confirmation of detailed needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Establish output objectives
description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). It includes agreeing the suitability of the proposed outputs and their quality measures with users. Legal or normative frameworks (e.g. relating to confidentiality, methodologies), and available resources are important to consider when establishing output objectives.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Output objectives must align with users' stated needs and consider quality, confidentiality, and resources. The Junior Evaluation Officer 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions' and 'supports the assessment of requirements for data', feeding into output suitability and quality objectives establishment.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 brings 'knowledge of socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, ... and results from alternative manipulations', contributing to defining meaningful and feasible output objectives and quality standards.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer ensures outputs can be documented and disseminated appropriately, with 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks', supporting the establishment of objectives that are both deliverable and properly described.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Identify concepts
description: This sub-process clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users. At this stage, the concepts identified might not align with existing statistical standards. This alignment, and the choice or definition of the statistical and other concepts and variables to be used, takes place in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Identification and clarification of concepts often requires analytical and subject matter expertise. Economist/Sociologist 2 is directly implicated because they 'analyze current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' and possess 'knowledge of socio-economic concepts and methods.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer assists by ensuring 'consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs'—ensuring that the identification of user concepts is framed with awareness of necessary metadata documentation and structural requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst supports this activity by 'organizing and consolidating information relevant to the defined objectives of studies', which may include definitions of new or revised measurement concepts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Check data availability and suitability
description: This sub-process checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. An assessment of possible alternatives would normally include research into potential administrative or other non-statistical sources of data (e.g. privately-held data or “Big Data”), to: Determine whether they would be suitable for use for statistical purposes (e.g. the extent to which administrative concepts match data requirements, and whether the timeliness and quality of the data, security, and continuity of data supply are suitable); Assess the division of responsibilities between data suppliers and the statistical organisation; Check necessary ICT resources (e.g. data storage, technology required to handle incoming data and data processing) as well as any provision agreements with data suppliers (which could be legal or other agreements such as memoranda of understanding) for accessing and sharing the data (e.g. formats, delivery, accompanying metadata and quality check). When existing sources have been assessed, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps in the data requirement is prepared. This may include identifying possible partnerships with data holders or conducting a new survey to collect data if necessary. This sub-process also includes a more general assessment of the legal framework in which data would be collected and used, and may therefore identify proposals for changes to existing legislation or the introduction of a new legal framework.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Evaluation Officer is experienced in 'conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data,' and 'collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources,' which is essential in assessing the availability and suitability of various types of data sources for user requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is involved in 'analyzing changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results' and 'knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability.' Their expertise is critical in assessing alternative data sources and their suitability.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst brings 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis', and supports in assessing data availability and quality for possible sources, including non-standard or administrative data.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Prepare and submit business case
description: This sub-process documents the findings of the other sub-processes in this phase, in the form of a business case to get approval to implement the new or modified statistical business process. Such a business case would need to conform to the requirements of the approval body, but would typically include elements such as: A description of the “As-Is” business process (if it already exists), with information on how the current statistics are produced, highlighting any inefficiencies and issues to be addressed; The proposed “To-Be” solution, detailing how the statistical business process will be developed to produce the new or revised statistics; An assessment of costs and benefits against objectives and any external constraints. The business case describes options and makes recommendations. It may include the benefits, costs, deliverables, time frame, budget, required technical and human resources, risk assessment and impact on stakeholders for each option. After the business case is prepared, it is submitted for approval to move to the next phase of the business process. At this sub-process, a “go”/“no go” decision is made. Typically, the business case is reviewed and formally approved or disapproved by the appropriate sponsors and governance committees.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Evaluation Officer 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management on elements of program evaluations', and 'undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as ... applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.' These activities provide direct support in the preparation and substantiation of a business case.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's 'writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science.' They contribute to the preparation of business case materials, supporting analysis, and visualization of findings.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Design
description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments and operational processes, with due regard to other requirements such as security. It includes all the design elements needed to define or refine the statistical products or services identified in the business case. This phase specifies all relevant metadata, in accordance with the standards and corporate policies, ready for use later in the business process, as well as quality assurance procedures. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration and whenever improvement actions are identified in the Evaluate phase of a previous iteration. Design activities make substantial use of international and national standards in order to reduce the length and cost of the design process, and enhance interoperability, comparability, etc. Organisations may reuse or adapt design elements from existing processes and consider geospatial aspects of data in the design to enhance the usability and value of the statistical information. Additionally, outputs of design processes may form the basis for future standards at the organisational, national or international levels. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Design phase requires subject matter knowledge, design of outputs and processes, and consideration of standards. The Economist/Sociologist 2, with their involvement in 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures', as well as 'assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities', is directly implicated throughout this design stage.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer's knowledge of 'systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows', together with input to 'training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery', makes them key contributors in developing and refining collection instruments and operational processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer is heavily implicated, as they 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata' and 'provide feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata'. Their knowledge ensures metadata standards are respected throughout design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst is directly involved via 'supporting the conduct of studies and/or projects', 'conducts data preparation techniques', and has 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture ... processing, ... modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization...' which aligns with design and refinement of statistical outputs, variables, and processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is engaged in 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases', participates in production teams, and drafts reports related to statistical data and methods, all of which support design iterations of outputs, quality measures, and dissemination infrastructure.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design outputs and dissemination
description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products and services to be produced, including the related systems, tools and procedures used in the Disseminate phase. Processes governing access to any confidential outputs are also designed here. Outputs should be designed to follow existing standards wherever possible, so inputs to this process may include metadata from similar or previous collections (including extractions from statistical, administrative, geospatial and other non-statistical registers and databases), international standards, and information about practices in other statistical organisations from sub-process 1.1 (Identify needs). Outputs may also be designed in partnership with other interested bodies, particularly if they are considered to be joint outputs, or they will be disseminated by another organisation.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is deeply involved in 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams', and so provides essential feedback and expertise for the detailed design of outputs, products, and dissemination procedures.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer ensures that outputs are documented with proper metadata, assists with 'statistical metadata quality evaluations', and 'provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals', helping design outputs that integrate compliance with metadata standards.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design variables
description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument, as well as any other variables that will be derived from them in sub-process 5.5 (Derive new variables and units), and any statistical or geospatial classifications that will be used. This is also where unit types (including observation units and statistical units) can be designed. It is expected that existing national and international standards will be followed wherever possible. This sub-process may need to run in parallel with sub-process 2.3 (Design collection), as the definition of the variables to be collected and the choice of collection instruments may be inter-dependent to some degree. Preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, statistical and geospatial classification is a necessary precondition for subsequent phases.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2, through 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, ... and presentation methods and procedures; ... and proposes changes or alternative systems', is essential to designing what variables will be collected, ensuring they have policy and analytical value.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer, via 'knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks' and experience 'preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata', ensures proper variable and classification design that supports metadata management and downstream use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's background in 'data preparation techniques, ... data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' supports the technical and quality aspects involved in defining new and derived variables.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Design collection
description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data, and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, which may depend on the type of data collection, the collection unit type (enterprise, person, or other) and the available sources of data. The actual activities in this sub-process will vary according to the type of collection instrument required, which can include computer assisted interviewing, paper questionnaires, administrative registers, automated and semi-automated data transfer methods (such as using APIs, machine-to-machine integrations and various types of file transfers), web-scraping technologies as well as technology for geospatial data. The collection may employ a multi-mode method which requires additional considerations such as design of sequencing or different instruments for different modes. Direct or indirect use of administrative data may be introduced in the data collection mode for either controlling survey data or assisting it when capturing survey information. In the case of survey (or census) data, this collection strategy includes the design of the collection instruments, questions and response templates (in conjunction with the variables and statistical classifications designed in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables)). It is important to understand respondents and incorporate the user perspectives in the design of data collection. This sub-process may include design of fieldwork operations, and respondent engagement, in the case of survey data collection. It also includes the confirmation of existing agreements or creation of new agreements. This sub-process is enabled by tools such as question libraries (to facilitate the reuse of questions and related attributes), questionnaire tools (to enable the quick and easy compilation of questions into formats suitable for cognitive testing) and agreement templates (to help standardise terms and conditions). This sub-process also includes the design of respondent management systems that are specific to this business process. Where statistical organisations do not collect data directly (i.e. a third party controls the collection and processing of the data), this sub-process may include the design of mechanisms to monitor the data and the metadata to assess impacts of any change made by the third party.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is vital for 'participating in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data', and for evaluating collection methods and procedures. This expertise is directly required for the design and evaluation of collection strategies and instruments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer brings 'knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data', ensuring that collection designs align with metadata and information quality requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design frame and sample
description: This sub-process applies especially to processes which involve data collection based on sampling, such as through statistical surveys, but it may also apply to other types of data collection such as census or register-based (e.g., filtering of registers based on the target population). It identifies and specifies the population of interest, defines a sampling frame (and, where necessary, the register from which it is derived), and determines the most appropriate sampling criteria and methodology (which could include complete enumeration). Common sources for a sampling frame are administrative and statistical registers, censuses and information from other sample surveys. It may refer to geospatial data and classifications. This sub-process describes how these sources can be combined if needed. Analysis of whether the frame covers the target population should be performed. Spatial analysis techniques can be used to ensure the spatial distribution of the units is appropriate. A sampling plan should be made. The actual sample is created in sub-process 4.1 (Create frame and select sample), using the methodology specified in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 contributes essential subject matter and methodological support, with their 'knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs', and ability to assess statistical validity of sampling frames and plans.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst, with understanding of 'statistical and mathematical principles', 'statistical sampling and cost benefit analysis', and experience with data preparation, helps design or validate sample and frame logic.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Design processing and analysis
description: This sub-process designs the statistical methodology to be applied during the Process and Analyse phases. This can include, among others, specification of routines and rules for coding, editing and imputation, which may vary based on the means of data collection and source of data. This subprocess also includes design of specifications for data integration from multiple data sources, validation of data and estimation. Statistical disclosure control methods are also designed here if they are specific to this business process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst is involved via 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle ... processing, mining, clustering, modeling', and 'conducts data preparation techniques ... in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality...', aligning with process and analysis method design for downstream phases.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer's participation in 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and evaluation of 'collection and coding methods, procedures and results' makes them directly tied to designing processing methodologies and supporting integration strategies.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2, with 'knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling', are central to specifying editing, imputation, and analysis routines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Design production systems and workflows
description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, taking an overview of all the processes required within the whole production process and ensuring that they fit together efficiently with no gaps or redundancies. Various systems and databases may be needed throughout the process. The GSBPM can be used to design a statistical organisation’s business architecture layer when a statistical organisation has an existing enterprise architecture in place. The design might be adjusted to fit the organisation. A general principle is to reuse processes and technology across many statistical business processes, so existing production solutions (e.g. services, systems and databases) should be examined first, to determine whether they are fit for purpose for this specific production process, then, if any gaps are identified, new solutions can be designed. This sub-process also considers how staff will interact with systems and who will be responsible for what and when.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is crucial in designing 'the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.' Their understanding of system design, operational requirements, and user interaction ensures workflows are realistic and robust.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer's experience with 'knowledge of the methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata' ensures system and workflow design supports correct metadata management across all phases.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Build
description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the “live” environment. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured in this phase to create the complete operational environment to run the process. New services are built by exception, created in response to gaps in the existing catalogue of services sourced from within the organisation and externally. These new services are constructed to be broadly reusable in alignment with the business architecture of the organisation where possible, and compliant with security requirements. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration, following a review or a change in methodology or technology, rather than for every iteration. The Build phase is broken down into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases. The first three sub-processes are concerned with the development and improvement of systems used in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data. The last four subprocesses focus on the end-to-end process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Build phase requires assembling, configuring, and testing production systems, including data collection, processing, and dissemination components. The Operations Officer, who 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' and 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers,' is directly involved in building and coordinating these systems for live use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer, with responsibilities to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata,' and to 'provide feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participate in the testing of new procedures and systems', is required to ensure metadata flows and integrations are assembled, tested, and validated in the build phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst supports the 'conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods', and has knowledge of 'data science and its life cycle, including ... warehousing, cleansing, processing, ... business intelligence, and exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis.' This knowledge and practice is necessary for contributing to the technical aspects of building and preparing analysis components for production.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Reuse or build collection instruments
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build and reuse the collection instruments needed during the Collect phase. The collection instruments are built based on the design specifications created during the Design phase. A collection may use one or more collection instruments to receive the data (e.g. personal or telephone interviews; paper, electronic or web questionnaires; SDMX web services). Collection instruments may also be data extraction routines used to gather data from existing statistical or administrative registers (e.g. by using existing service interfaces). This sub-process also includes preparing and testing the contents and functioning of that collection instrument (e.g. cognitive testing of the questions in a questionnaire). It is recommended to consider the direct connection of collection instruments to a metadata system, so that metadata can be more easily captured in the collection phase. Connecting metadata and data at the point of capture can save work in later phases. Capturing the metrics of data collection (paradata) is also an important consideration in this sub-process for calculating and analysing process quality indicators.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is directly involved due to their responsibility to 'participate in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.' Building and testing collection instruments (questionnaires, data extraction routines, etc.) directly requires their experience.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer's role includes 'assisting with statistical metadata quality evaluations and providing input to reports for clients and management,' which is essential for ensuring collection instruments are both functional and properly integrated with metadata systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new components needed for the Process and Analyse phases, as designed in the Design phase. Services (re-)used may include dashboard functions and features, information services, transformation functions, geospatial data services, workflow management tools, respondent and metadata management services.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's expertise in 'conducting data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation', is necessary for setting up and testing analysis and processing components (such as dashboards, transformation and validation routines) as required for data processing and analysis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer 'assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers', helping determine if new or existing components are needed and suitable, and supports their integration.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Reuse or build dissemination components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new components or reuse existing components needed for the dissemination of statistical products as designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination). All types of dissemination components are included, from those that produce traditional paper publications to those that provide web services, (linked) open data outputs, geospatial statistics, maps, or access to microdata.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is responsible for 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', and their expertise in disseminating via various components (tables, charts, files, microdata) aligns with building and validating appropriate dissemination infrastructure and tools.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer supports proper dissemination by ensuring 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata', so that dissemination components correctly present both data and metadata for users.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Configure workflows
description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems and transformations used within the business processes, from data collection through to dissemination. In this sub-process, the workflows are configured based on the design created in sub-process 2.6 (Design production systems and workflows). This could include modifying a standardised workflow for a specific purpose, assembling the workflows for the different phases together (possibly with a workflow/business process management system) and configuring systems accordingly.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is closely involved, as they 'meet with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur' and 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.' This expertise is indispensable in configuring and modifying workflows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Test production systems
description: This sub-process is concerned with the testing of assembled and configured services and related workflows. It includes technical testing and sign-off of new programmes and routines, as well as confirmation that existing routines from other statistical business processes are suitable for use in this case. Whilst part of this activity concerning the testing of individual components and services could logically be linked with sub-processes 3.1 (Reuse or build collection instruments), 3.2 (Reuse or build processing and analysis components) and 3.3 (Reuse or build dissemination components), this sub-process also includes testing of interactions between assembled and configured services and ensuring that the whole production solution works in a coherent way. It can also include arranging secure channels for the transmission of the data, checking detailed information about files and metadata with a data supplier and receiving test files to assess if data are fit for use.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer's expertise in reviewing, evaluating and testing operational procedures and systems is essential for technical and user acceptance testing. Their role includes 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives' and prepares documentation and reports that would be part of test, debugging, and acceptance processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer's responsibility to 'participate in the testing of new procedures and systems' ensures that systems reflect correct metadata requirements, and the successful integration of metadata handling is verified in production testing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Test statistical business process
description: This sub-process describes the activities to manage a field test or pilot of the statistical business process. Typically, it includes a small-scale data collection, to test the collection instruments, followed by processing and analysis of the collected data, to ensure the statistical business process performs as expected. Following the pilot, it may be necessary to go back to a previous step and make adjustments to collection instruments, systems or components. For a major statistical business process, e.g. a population census, there may be several iterations until the process is working satisfactorily.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer directly supports pilot and field testing, given their involvement in 'participating in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.' Their experience is essential for identifying practical challenges and refining instruments post-pilot.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst supports process and outcome evaluation of pilots with skills in 'organizing and consolidating information relevant to the defined objectives of studies' and applying quantitative methods to review pilot analysis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Finalise production systems
description: This sub-process includes the activities to put the assembled and configured processes and services, including modified and newly-created services, into production ready for use. The activities include: Producing documentation about the process components, including technical documentation and user manuals; Training the users of the system on how to operate the process; Moving the process components into the production environment and ensuring they work as expected in that environment (this activity may also be part of sub-process 3.5 (Test production systems).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is responsible for preparing 'survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports', and 'assists in training delivery'—these responsibilities are core for finalizing systems, producing documentation, and training users.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer provides input to 'documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata and assists with the delivery of training', ensuring all metadata elements are managed in finalized system documentation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Collect
description: This phase collects or gathers all necessary information (e.g. data, metadata and paradata), using different collection approaches (e.g. acquisition, collection, extraction, transfer), and loads them into the appropriate environment for further processing. Whilst it can include validation of data set formats, it does not include any transformations of the data themselves, as these are all done in the Process phase. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The Collect phase is broken down into four sub-processes (Figure 10), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is directly implicated in all aspects of data collection, as they 'participate in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data', 'provide assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection', and 'participate on data collection and operations teams.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst supports data collection through 'conducts data preparation techniques ... in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and 'participates in project teams and working groups to support data management.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Create frame and select sample
description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). It also includes the coordination of samples between instances of the same business process (e.g. to manage overlap or rotation), and between different processes using a common frame or register (e.g. to manage overlap or to spread response burden). Quality assurance and approval of the frame and the selected sample are also undertaken in this sub-process, though maintenance of underlying registers, from which frames for several statistical business processes are drawn, is treated as a separate activity. The sampling aspect of this sub-process is often not relevant for processes based entirely on the use of preexisting sources (e.g. administrative sources and other non-survey sources) as such processes generally create frames from the available data and then follow a census approach. Variables from administrative and other non-statistical sources of data can be used as auxiliary variables in the construction of sampling design.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition,' and 'statistical sampling and cost benefit analysis' directly relate to creating frames and selecting appropriate samples. They would also organize and manage the extracted data for sampling operations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer's involvement in 'the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'knowledge of statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data' make them essential for quality assurance and managing operational frame/sample work.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Set up collection
description: This sub-process ensures that the people, processes and technology (e.g. web-based applications, devices to be used in collection, communication channels) are ready to collect data and metadata, as designed. It takes place over a period of time, as it includes the strategy, planning and training activities in preparation for the specific instance of the statistical business process. Where the process is repeated regularly, some (or all) of these activities may not be explicitly required for each iteration. For one-off and new processes, these activities can be lengthy. For survey data, this sub-process includes: Training collection staff; Training system using supervised machine learning techniques; Ensuring collection resources are available (e.g. collection devices, apps, APIs); Agreeing on terms with any intermediate collection bodies, (e.g. sub-contractors for computer assisted telephone interviewing, web service providers); Configuring collection systems to request and receive the data, including location data; Ensuring the security of data to be collected; Preparing collection instruments (e.g. printing questionnaires, pre-filling them with existing data, loading questionnaires and data onto interviewers' devices/computers, APIs, web scraping tools); Providing information for respondents (e.g. drafting letters/emails to respondents, credentials, guidance or tailored information to address questions they may have, or notifying respondents when online reporting instruments will be made available); Translation of materials (e.g. into the different languages spoken or used in the country). For non-survey sources, this sub-process ensures that the necessary processes, systems and confidentiality procedures are in place, to receive or extract the necessary information from the source. This includes: Evaluating requests to obtain the data and logging the request in a centralised inventory; Initiating contacts with organisations providing the data, and sending an introductory package with details on the process of obtaining the data; Routine checks that the system is working as expected.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer, 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for data collection' and 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection.' They also 'provide input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assist in training delivery', directly supporting collection set-up and operational readiness.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Run collection
description: This sub-process is where the collection is implemented. The different collection instruments are used to collect or gather the information, which may include raw microdata or aggregates produced at the source, as well as any associated metadata. For survey or census data, it can include: Initial contact with respondents to request data and any subsequent follow-up or reminder actions, recording when and how they were contacted, and whether they have reacted; Management of the relationship between the statistical organisation and respondents, so that it remains positive, and recording and responding to comments, queries and complaints. (Minimisation of the number of non-respondents contributes significantly to higher quality of the collected data.); Manual data entry at the point of contact, or fieldwork management, depending on the source and collection approach; Georeferencing at the same time as collection of the data (using inputs from location-enabled systems such as GPS), or recording location by putting a mark on a map, etc., depending on the geographical frame and the technology used. Automated logical checks on data at the point of collection (i.e. validation-on-entry for survey response data) are considered to take place in 5.3 (Review and validate). For administrative, geospatial, or other non-statistical data, the data supplier either sends it as scheduled or is contacted to send the information, which might require follow-ups. Broader technical-level engagement with data suppliers falls under the Data Supplier Management overarching activity. In the case where the data are published under an Open Data license and exist in machine-readable form, they may be freely accessed and used. This sub-process may also include the monitoring of data collection and making any necessary changes to improve data quality. This includes generating reports, visualising and adjusting the process for obtaining data to ensure the data are fit for use. When the collection meets its targets, it is closed and a report on the collection is produced. Some basic checks of the structure and integrity of the information received may take place within this sub-process, (e.g. checking that files are in the right format and contain the expected fields).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer is heavily involved in 'manual data entry at the point of contact' and in managing 'the collection, coding and processing of data', providing direct support for running and overseeing the actual collection process, including troubleshooting and maintaining collection flow.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst, by 'supporting studies/projects', 'conducting data preparation techniques', and 'participating in project teams ... to support data management', may be called on to assist in managing, troubleshooting, and validating data as it is collected.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Finalise collection
description: This sub-process includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing. It may include manual or automatic data capture, for example, using clerical staff or optical character recognition tools to extract information from paper questionnaires, or converting the formats of files or encoding the variables received from other organisations. It may also include analysis of the metadata and paradata associated with collection to ensure the collection activities have met requirements. In cases where there is a physical collection instrument, such as a paper questionnaire, which is not needed for further processing, this sub-process manages the archiving of that material. When the collection instrument uses software such as an API or an app, this sub-process also includes the versioning and archiving of these. The data could be pseudonymised at this stage before further processing.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer, with responsibility for 'manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and producing 'reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection systems', is directly implicated in data loading, conversion, and archiving, ensuring readiness for downstream processing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst, with duties to 'organize and consolidate information relevant to the defined objectives of studies' and knowledge in 'data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, and data stewardship', will participate in the proper transfer, organization, and quality checking of finalized collection datasets.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Process
description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis. It is made up of sub-processes that integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data, so that they can be analysed and disseminated as statistical outputs. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The sub-processes in this phase can apply to data from both statistical and non-statistical sources (with the possible exception of sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights), which is usually specific to survey data). Some variables could be processed prior to others if they are required for data integration (e.g., geospatial variables if used for that purpose). The Process and Analyse phases can be iterative and parallel. Analysis can reveal a broader understanding of the data, which might make it apparent that additional processing is needed. Sometimes the estimates being processed might be already published aggregates (undertaken according to a Revision Policy). Activities within the Process and Analyse phases may also commence before the Collect phase is completed. This enables the compilation of provisional results where timeliness is an important concern for users, and increases the time available for analysis. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst is directly implicated in all core process activities—integrating, cleaning, validating, transforming, and preparing data for analysis. Their duties include 'conducts data preparation techniques ... in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' matching the requirements of this phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer, who participates in the 'collection, coding and processing of data', and has 'knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications', is needed for process operations that enable the transition from raw to analysis-ready data.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Integrate data
description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources. It is where the results of subprocesses in the Collect phase are combined. The input data can be from a mixture of external or internal sources, and a variety of collection instruments, including extracts of administrative and other non-statistical data sources. Administrative data or other non-statistical sources of data can substitute for all or some of the variables directly collected from a survey. This sub-process also includes harmonising or creating new figures that agree between sources of data. The result is a consolidated set of data. Data integration can include: Combining data from multiple sources, as part of the creation of integrated statistics such as national accounts; Combining geospatial data and statistical data or other non-statistical data; Data pooling, with the aim of increasing the effective number of observations of some phenomena; Matching or record linkage routines, with the aim of linking micro or macro data from different sources; Data fusion - integration followed by reduction or replacement; Prioritising, when two or more sources contain data for the same variable, with potentially different values. Data integration may take place at any point in this phase, before or after any of the other subprocesses. There may also be several instances of data integration in any statistical business process. Following integration, depending on data protection requirements, data may be deidentified, that is stripped of identifiers such as name and address, to help to protect confidentiality.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's knowledge of 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, ... and exploratory/confirmatory analysis' is needed for integrating data from varying sources, performing record linkage, and harmonizing disparate files.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer, with experience in 'the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'knowledge of data sources and contacts', is directly engaged in coordinating source integration and ensuring process reliability across different data feeds.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Classify and code
description: This sub-process classifies and codes the input data. For example, automatic (or clerical) coding routines may assign numeric codes to text responses according to a pre-determined statistical classification to facilitate data capture and processing. Some questions have coded response categories on the questionnaires or administrative source of data, others are coded after collection using an automated process (which may apply machine learning or artificial intelligence techniques) or an interactive, manual process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer's role in 'participates in the ... coding and processing of data', as well as 'evaluates collection and coding methods', directly aligns with the technical and operational responsibilities of classifying and coding input data as required for standardization and downstream use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst applies 'data preparation techniques ... including data cleansing, processing, ... and quantitative analysis' to supporting automated or manual coding of classifications, meeting requirements for valid transformation and standardized codes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Review and validate
description: This sub-process examines data to identify potential problems, errors and discrepancies such as outliers, item non-response, miscoding and duplicate records. It can also be referred to as input data validation. It may be run iteratively, validating data against pre-defined edit rules, usually in a set order. It may flag data for automatic or manual inspection or editing. Reviewing and validating can apply to data from any type of source, before and after integration, as well as imputed data from sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute). Whilst validation is treated as part of the Process phase, in practice, some elements of validation may occur alongside collection activities, particularly for approaches such as computer assisted collection. Whilst this sub-process is concerned with detection and localisation of actual or potential errors, any correction activities that actually change the data is done in sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's responsibilities include 'data validation' and 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.' This is essential for reviewing and validating the integrity, structure, and correctness of datasets at this stage.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer applies 'knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.' Their active role in quality assurance fits directly with this sub-process of input validation and error detection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Edit and impute
description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, new values may be inserted, or erroneous data may be removed in this sub-process. The terms editing and imputation cover a variety of methods to do this, often using a rule-based approach. Specific steps typically include: Determining whether to add or change data; Selecting the method to be used; Adding/changing data values; Writing the new data values back to the data set, and flagging them as changed; Producing metadata on the editing and imputation process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst, through their work in 'data cleansing, processing, and transformation,' may be involved in identifying missing or erroneous values and applying standard protocols for editing and imputation, ensuring completeness and reliability of the data.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer, by 'participating in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for ... processing of data' and using their 'knowledge of statistical concepts', supports systematic editing and imputation activities, both automated and manual.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Derive new variables and units
description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units that are not explicitly provided in the collection, but are needed to deliver the required outputs. It derives new variables by applying arithmetic formulae to one or more of the variables that are already present in the dataset, or applying different model assumptions. This activity may need to be iterative, as some derived variables may themselves be based on other derived variables. It is therefore important to ensure that variables are derived in the correct order. New units may be derived by aggregating or splitting data for collection units, or by various other estimation methods. Examples include deriving households where the collection units are persons or enterprises where the collection units are legal units.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, ... modeling, summarization, reporting, ... regression, ... and quantitative analysis', enables them to derive new statistical variables and aggregations as required in this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Calculate weights
description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records according to the methodology developed in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). For example, weights can be used to “gross up” data to make them representative of the target population (e.g. for sample surveys or extracts of scanner data), or to adjust for non-response in total enumerations. In other situations, variables may need weighting for normalisation purposes. It may also include weight correction for benchmarking indicators (e.g. known population totals).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst, with 'knowledge of statistical and mathematical principles' and 'statistical sampling and cost benefit analysis', supports calculation and application of weights for survey data and may automate or validate the weighting process using statistical packages.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Calculate aggregates
description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates. It includes summing data for records sharing certain characteristics (e.g. aggregation of data by demographic or geographic classifications), determining measures of average and dispersion, and applying weights from sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights) to derive appropriate totals. In the case of statistical outputs which use sample surveys, sampling errors corresponding to relevant aggregates may also be calculated in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's work in 'clustering, modeling, summarization, ... reporting, ... regression, ... and quantitative analysis,' is essential for aggregating microdata, computing statistics, and preparing population totals as per methodological standards.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Finalise data files
description: This sub-process brings together the results of the other sub-processes in this phase in a data set (either micro- or macro-data), which is used as the input to the Analyse phase. Sometimes, this may be an intermediate rather than a final data set, particularly for business processes where there are strong time pressures, and a requirement to produce both preliminary and final estimates.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst supports the preparation and versioning of finalized datasets for analysis, relying on skills to 'organize and consolidate information relevant to the defined objectives of studies', and ensuring the correct data structures and documentation are delivered for downstream analysis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Operations Officer, experienced in reviewing 'data sources and outputs to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results,' and preparing technical documentation, contributes to data integrity checking and documentation before passing data to analysis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Analyse
description: In this phase, statistical outputs are produced and examined in detail. It includes preparing statistical content (including commentary, technical notes, etc.), and ensuring outputs are “fit for purpose” prior to dissemination to users. This phase also includes the sub-processes and activities that enable statistical analysts to understand the data and the statistics produced. The outputs of this phase could also be used as an input to other sub-processes (e.g. analysis of new sources as input to the Design phase). For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in every iteration. The Analyse phase and sub-processes are generic for all statistical outputs, regardless of how the data were sourced. The Analyse phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 12), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 is directly implicated as they 'participate in the analysis of statistical program data and assist in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes', 'identify statistical trends and developments', and 'participate in the analysis of data and suggest possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods.' Their experience ensures statistical outputs are comprehensively analyzed and meet user needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst is responsible for 'supporting the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods,' and for 'draft[ing] clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material.' Their skills are critical for core analytical work, preparing materials, interpreting data, and verifying quality.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Prepare draft outputs
description: This sub-process is where the data from sub-processes 5.7 (Calculate aggregates) and 5.8 (Finalise data files) are transformed into statistical outputs, which could include indexes, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, microdata, etc. The preparation of maps, GIS outputs and geo-statistical services can be included to maximise the value and capacity to analyse the statistical information. Methodological notes, to accompany the outputs and describe how they have been produced are also prepared in this sub-process taking as input the methodology designed in the Design phase. When new processing or analysis methods such as those based on machine learning or artificial intelligence are used, additional explanations might need to be prepared to communicate/explain the necessary information to the users.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst is responsible for 'conducting studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods', and 'draft[ing] analytical reports'—skills needed to transform processed data into structured outputs, create indexes and mapped data, and prepare methodological notes for publication.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 'assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes' and brings 'knowledge of statistical or economic theory ... and methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling', necessary for preparing outputs and methodological notes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Validate outputs
description: This sub-process is where statisticians validate the outputs produced, in accordance with a general quality framework and with expectations and also comparing with auxiliary information available (e.g. from previous cycles or from other sources). This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst's activities include 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin' and 'draft[ing] clear and simple analytical reports ... using data visualization tools' that help verify the outputs in relation to supporting data, previous cycles, and internal standards.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 'assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored,' providing essential knowledge for validation against expectations and previously observed patterns.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Interpret and explain outputs
description: This sub-process is where outputs are interpreted in order to understand their meaning and to try to explain them. This can involve viewing the statistics from all perspectives using different tools and media, and carrying out various types of in-depth analysis to gain insight into the results and assess them against initial expectations, based also on an understanding of how those results were produced. Such analyses might include time series analysis and other econometric analyses, etc.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2's main duties include 'identifying statistical trends and developments,' 'analysis of statistical program data,' and preparing explanatory and analytic content for programs—these directly align with interpreting and explaining outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
