implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst, who 'drafts clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients,' is responsible for organizing, interpreting, and clearly communicating analytical findings and output explanations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Apply disclosure control
description: This sub-process ensures that the data (and metadata) to be disseminated or internally stored for future use do not breach the appropriate rules on confidentiality according to either organisational policies and rules, or to the process-specific methodology created in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). This may include checks for primary and secondary disclosure, as well as the application of data suppression or perturbation techniques and output checking. The degree and method of statistical disclosure control may vary for different types of outputs. For example, the approach used for microdata sets for research purposes will be different to that for published tables or visualisations at the aggregated level. Geospatial data or outputs from geospatial data may raise additional confidentiality challenges in terms of personal data protection and disclosure risk.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer's key activities include 'edits, validates, ... and disseminates data', with 'knowledge of the Statistics Act and of Statistics Canada policies, directives and guidelines in order to ensure understanding and application of the Act and these policies, directives and guidelines in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data.' They are directly responsible for applying disclosure control and ensuring outputs comply with confidentiality standards.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst has 'data literacy skills ... to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use', equipping them to perform disclosure control checks on outputs and metadata before dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Finalise outputs
description: This sub-process ensures the statistics and associated information are fit for purpose and reach the required quality level and are thus ready for use. It includes: Completing consistency checks; Determining the level of release, and applying caveats; Collating supporting information, including interpretation, commentary, technical notes, briefings, measures of uncertainty and any other necessary metadata; Producing the supporting internal documents; Conducting pre-release discussion with appropriate internal subject matter experts; Translating the statistical outputs in countries with multilingual dissemination; Approving the statistical content for release.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Data Analyst contributes by 'draft[ing] clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools', 'organizing and consolidating information relevant to the defined objectives of studies', and validating outputs for release — clearly supporting the preparation, review, and documentation of statistical outputs for release.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 'assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes', and 'writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs', which contribute to final output approval and supporting documentation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Disseminate
description: This phase manages the release of the statistical data and their products to users. It includes all activities associated with assembling and releasing a range of static and dynamic products via a range of channels. These activities support users to access and use the products released by the statistical organisation. For statistical products produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. Cataloguing and tagging released data and products using relevant metadata standards can greatly increase their discoverability and accessibility both internally and externally. International standards should be used as a norm to ensure that they can be found and consumed easily across a broad range of users. Linking data to geospatial classifications in particular can allow for detailed geographical presentation of outputs. While GSBPM conceives of archiving as taking place within the overarching Data Management and Metadata Management activities, its relevance to finalised outputs in this phase should be noted. The Disseminate phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is centrally responsible for 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', 'interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations', and participates on 'data production and dissemination teams'. These activities are at the heart of assembling, releasing, and supporting statistical products as part of dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata' and participates in 'the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata', ensuring that metadata standards and cataloguing requirements are met for product discovery and user support.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Update output systems
description: This sub-process manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes, including: Formatting data and metadata ready to be put into output systems; Loading data and metadata into output systems; Ensuring data are linked to the relevant metadata. Formatting, loading and linking of metadata should preferably mostly take place in earlier phases, but this sub-process includes a final check that all of the necessary metadata are in place ready for dissemination.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer's core duties are to 'prepare, edit, validate and disseminate statistical metadata', offer 'input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals', and ensure correct metadata management. Their oversight is required to update, link, and validate all data/metadata in output systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer, who 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases', is necessary to ensure the technical loading, formatting, and quality evaluation of disseminated data objects, readying them for user consumption.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Produce dissemination products
description: This sub-process produces the dissemination products, as previously designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination), to meet user needs. They could include publications, press releases and websites. The products can take many forms including interactive graphics, tables, maps, public-use microdata sets, linked open data and downloadable files. When the final products raise concern for confidentiality, additional disclosure control may be considered and applied via sub-process 6.4 (Apply disclosure control). Typical steps include: Preparing the product components (explanatory texts, tables, charts, maps, quality statements etc.); Assembling the components into products; Editing the products and checking that they meet publication standards.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is directly responsible for 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', and for 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.' They assemble, edit, and finalize all statistical products for external audiences.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Release dissemination products
description: This sub-process ensures that all elements for the release are in place including managing the timing of the release. It includes briefings for specific groups such as the press or ministers, as well as the arrangements for any pre-release embargoes. It also includes the provision of products to subscribers, and managing access to confidential data by authorised user groups, such as researchers. Sometimes an organisation may need to retract a product, for example, if an error is discovered. This is also included in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer manages and coordinates the timed and secure release of products, utilizing their experience in 'disseminates data', and preparing product releases, as well as 'drafts program information manuals and training packages for use by colleagues, operational staff and management, and assists in the delivery of training.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Promote dissemination products
description: Whilst marketing in general can be considered to be part of GAMSO, this sub-process concerns the active promotion of the statistical products produced in a specific statistical business process, to help them reach the widest possible audience. It includes the use of customer relationship management tools, to better target potential users of the products, as well as the use of tools including websites and other platforms like social media to facilitate the process of communicating statistical information to users. These activities may be coordinated with partners in the case of joint products.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is implicated through their activities to 'markets ... and disseminates data' and through participation in data production and dissemination teams, ensuring broad uptake of statistical information using appropriate channels and tools.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Provide user support
description: This sub-process ensures that user queries and requests for services such as microdata access are recorded, and that responses are provided within agreed deadlines. These queries and requests should be regularly reviewed to provide an input to the overarching Quality Management activity, as they can indicate new or changing user needs. Replies to user requests can also be used to populate a knowledge database or a “Frequently Asked Questions” page, that is made publicly available, thus reducing the burden of replying to repeated and/or similar requests from external users. This sub-process also includes managing support to any partner organisations involved in disseminating the products.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Officer is engaged in 'provides statistical data and consultative services to users', and their expertise in responding to user requests ensures queries, knowledge management, and FAQ updates are correctly handled.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer, by 'provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies', and 'participates on teams tasked with the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata', ensures user support regarding metadata, standards, and use of statistical outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Evaluate
description: This phase manages the evaluation of a specific instance of a statistical business process, as opposed to the more general overarching activity of Quality Management described in Section V (Descriptions of overarching activities). It can take place at the end of the instance of the process, but can also be done on an ongoing basis during the statistical production process. It relies on inputs gathered throughout the different phases. It includes evaluating the success of a specific instance of the statistical business process, drawing on a range of quantitative and qualitative inputs, and identifying and prioritising potential improvements. For statistical outputs produced regularly, evaluation should, at least in theory, occur for each iteration, determining whether future iterations should take place, and if so, whether any improvements should be implemented. However, in some cases, particularly for regular and wellestablished statistical business processes, evaluation might not be formally carried out for each iteration. In such cases, this phase can be seen as providing the decision as to whether the next iteration should start from the Specify Needs phase, or from some later phase (often the Collect phase). The Evaluate phase is broken down into three sub-processes (Figure 14), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Evaluation Officer is central to evaluation, as their work includes 'participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies', 'provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data', 'conducts analyses and interpretation of data collected during evaluation studies', and helps 'formulat[e] conclusions' and recommendations. These functions directly address the review and improvement focus of this phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 'participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers' and 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' Their experience is vital for evaluating program performance and recommending improvements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer's responsibilities explicitly include 'provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems', ensuring that metadata and process quality evaluation are included in statistical process review.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Gather evaluation inputs
description: Evaluation material can be produced in any other phase or sub-process. It may take many forms, including feedback from users, process metadata (paradata), system metrics, and staff suggestions. Reports of progress against an action plan agreed during a previous iteration may also form an input to evaluations of subsequent iterations. This sub-process gathers all of these inputs, compiles quality indicators and makes them available for the person or team producing the evaluation. The collection of some of these evaluation materials can be automated and take place in a continuous way throughout the whole process, as defined by the quality framework (see Quality Management in Section V). On the other hand, for the evaluation of certain processes it can be necessary to perform specific activities such as small surveys, (e.g. post-enumeration surveys, re-interview studies, survey on effectiveness of dissemination).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Evaluation Officer 'collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources, including interviews, departmental documents and those of other government departments, as well as information from provincial and territorial governments and the Internet.' This is directly relevant to gathering evaluation inputs from diverse sources for process review.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer is involved in 'prepar[ing], edit[ing], validat[ing] and disseminat[ing] statistical metadata,' and assisting with 'statistical metadata quality evaluations ... input to reports for clients and management,' supporting the collection and review of process and metadata-related evaluation inputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Conduct evaluation
description: This sub-process analyses the evaluation inputs, compares them to the expected/target benchmarking results (when available), and synthesises them into an evaluation report or control dashboard. The evaluation can take place at the end of the whole process (ex-post evaluation), for selected activities, during its execution in a continuous way, or throughout the process, thus allowing for quick fixes or continuous improvement. The resulting report should note any quality issues specific to this iteration of the statistical business process as well as highlighting any deviation of performance metrics from expected values, and should make recommendations for changes if appropriate. These recommendations can cover changes to any phase or sub-process for future iterations of the process, or can suggest that the process is not repeated.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Evaluation Officer 'conducts analyses and interpretation of data collected during evaluation studies', 'applies analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulates conclusions,' and 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports.' These are direct requirements for synthesizing evaluation inputs, benchmarking, and preparing evaluation reports.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Economist/Sociologist 2 contributes by 'analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.' This aligns with reviewing metrics and performance, analyzing findings, and forming recommendations for improvement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Agree an action plan
description: This sub-process brings together the necessary decision-making power to form and agree an action plan based on the evaluation report. It should also include consideration of a mechanism for monitoring the impact of those actions, which may, in turn, provide an input to evaluations of future iterations of the process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Junior Evaluation Officer is responsible for 'provid[ing] input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations', and 'recommends ... enhancements to methods for retrieving data.' Their analytical support and recommendations are integral to forming improvement action plans based on evaluations.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer
